CodeRabbit CLI - Install Guide CodeRabbit’s CLI runs AI code review on your local repo before you commit. Catches hallucinated function calls, off-by-one bugs, missing tests, hardcoded secrets, race conditions. The kind of stuff Claude or Cursor will generate and you’d ship without noticing. Free to start. This guide is the cleaned-up version of what I actually went through to get it running on Windows. Windows (via WSL) The official install path on Windows is through WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux). Ten minutes if WSL is already set up, longer if you have to enable it. macOS and Linux are easier — skip to the bottom section for those. 1. En able WSL if it’s n o t already run n in g Open PowerShell as Administrator and run: w s l - - s t a t u s If it prints kernel info, skip to step 2. If you see a service error (“service cannot be started, either because it is disabled… ”), the W s l S e r v i c e is disabled. Enable it: S e t - S e r v i c e - N a m e W s l S e r v i c e - S t a r t u p T y p e M a n u a l S t a r t - S e r v i c e - N a m e W s l S e r v i c e If w s l isn’t recognized at all, install it: w s l - - i n s t a l l - d U b u n t u - - w e b - d o w n l o a d Reboot when it finishes. On first launch, Ubuntu prompts you for a username and password — pick anything memorable. 2. In stall the missin g p rereq The CodeRabbit install script needs u n z i p , which isn’t in fresh Ubuntu by default. Install it once: w s l - d U b u n t u - - u s e r r o o t - - a p t - g e t u p d a t e - q q w s l - d U b u n t u - - u s e r r o o t - - a p t - g e t i n s t a l l - y u n z i p 3. In stall C o deRabbit C LI Open a WSL terminal (type w s l in PowerShell, or open Ubuntu from Start menu), then run: c u r l - f s S L h t t p s : / / c l i . c o d e r a b b i t . a i / i n s t a l l . s h | s h The script installs to ~ / . l o c a l / b i n / c o d e r a b b i t and adds it to your PATH in ~ / . b a s h r c . Reload your shell so it picks up the new PATH: s o u r c e ~ / . b a s h r c Verify the install: c o d e r a b b i t - - v e r s i o n You should see something like 0 . 4 . 5 .

Verify: c o d e r a b b i t a u t h s t a t u s Should show L o g g e d i n plus your account details. 5. Run yo ur first review Navigate into a git repo with some uncommitted changes: c d / m n t / c / p a t h / t o / y o u r / r e p o c o d e r a b b i t r e v i e w Default mode is - - p l a i n (text findings stream to terminal). Other modes: • c o d e r a b b i t r e v i e w - - i n t e r a c t i v e — full-screen TUI, arrow keys navigate findings, Enter to expand • c o d e r a b b i t r e v i e w - - a g e n t — JSON output for piping into other tools macOS / Linux Single command sequence: c u r l - f s S L h t t p s : / / c l i . c o d e r a b b i t . a i / i n s t a l l . s h | s h s o u r c e ~ / . b a s h r c # o r ~ / . z s h r c i f y o u u s e z s h c o d e r a b b i t a u t h l o g i n c o d e r a b b i t r e v i e w No WSL, no unzip prereq. Done. Common gotchas Review han gs o n “Settin g up ” First run of c o d e r a b b i t r e v i e w auto-adds an o r i g i n remote pointing to g i t h u b . c o m / < y o u r - u s e r n a m e > / < f o l d e r - n a m e > . g i t and writes c o d e r a b b i t . d e f a u l t b r a n c h = m a i n to . g i t / c o n f i g . If that GitHub repo doesn’t exist, g i t - r e m o t e - h t t p s will hang for minutes trying to fetch it. Fix: g i t r e m o t e r e m o v e o r i g i n g i t c o n f i g - - u n s e t c o d e r a b b i t . d e f a u l t b r a n c h Then retry the review. “Limited / free C LI behavio r” ban n er This appears when your local repo isn’t tied to a CodeRabbit org install on GitHub. The review still works but is rate-limited. To remove it: 1. Push your repo to GitHub: g h r e p o c r e a t e y o u r - r e p o - n a m e - - p r i v a t e - - s o u r c e = . - - r e m o t e = o r i g i n - - p u s h

2. Go to h t t p s : / / a p p . c o d e r a b b i t . a i / s e t t i n g s / r e p o s i t o r i e s 3. Click “Add Repository” and install the CodeRabbit GitHub App on the repo you just pushed 4. Run c o d e r a b b i t r e v i e w again — the banner is gone and reviews run faster “co derabbit: co mman d n o t fo un d” after in stall The install adds the PATH update to ~ / . b a s h r c . If your terminal session was already open before the install ran, it hasn’t re-read the file. Two fixes: • One-time: s o u r c e ~ / . b a s h r c • Or just close the terminal and open a new one — any new shell picks up the change automatically Useful flags • - - t y p e u n c o m m i t t e d — review only uncommitted (staged + unstaged) changes • - - t y p e c o m m i t t e d — review only changes already committed on your current branch • - - b a s e < b r a n c h > — compare against a specific base branch instead of HEAD • - - d i r < p a t h > — review a different directory (must contain a git repo) • - - n o - c o l o r — disable terminal color codes (useful for CI logs) Where to go from here The CLI is the local-dev surface. CodeRabbit also runs as a GitHub App that reviews PRs automatically — install it on your repos at a p p . c o d e r a b b i t . a i / s e t t i n g s / r e p o s i t o r i e s to get the same review on every pull request you open. Try CodeRabbit at: c o d e r a b b i t . l i n k / m i r k o v i c d e v
